best_for: Gamers who own an original Xbox and its games and want to play them on a PC or Mac at higher resolution, with save states and modern controllers.

points.title: You must supply the Xbox files
points.text: xemu needs an MCPX boot ROM and a BIOS image, and the project does not provide them. The only legal source it names is dumping them from your own Xbox. A stock retail BIOS will not boot games; it needs a debug or modded one.

points.title: A blank hard disk is offered
points.text: The project offers a ready-made 8 GB hard disk image with no copyrighted content. Its dashboard is a basic unsigned one, not Microsoft's.

points.title: Sharper than the original
points.text: Render scaling lifts games from 480p up to 1080p, and you can change it while playing. Save states let you stop and resume anywhere.

points.title: Controllers and online play
points.text: Up to four controllers work at once through SDL3. Networking links xemu to other copies or real Xboxes, locally or over the internet through tunneling services.

points.title: Game support varies
points.text: Volunteers report how well each title runs, and the project warns those reports can be out of date. Check your game before you count on it.

points.title: Builds for every desktop
points.text: Windows builds come as zips for x64 and Arm64, the Mac build is universal, and the Flathub package is published by the xemu project and marked verified. It is free under the GPL-2.0.

points.title: Frequent releases
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 154 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source. The Flatpak here is at 0.8.136, a little behind the 0.8.139 Windows and Mac builds.
